title: Not to be seen (Matthew 6:1–6)
hook: give, pray and fast in secret; your Father sees in secret

segments.voice: Yesterday, love your enemies, and your line was the sun shines on all. Did you wish someone difficult a little sunlight? Day two hundred forty-eight.

Have you ever done something kind and then felt the tiny itch to post about it? A donation, a volunteer shift, a good deed. Just a small photo. Just so people know. Most of us have felt that pull. There's nothing new about it. Now Jesus turns to the three great practices of his people's faith: giving to the poor, praying and fasting. He doesn't say don't do them. He assumes you will. He asks something sharper: who are you doing them for?
screen: `THE ITCH TO POST IT.` → `GIVING, PRAYING, FASTING.` → `WHO ARE YOU DOING IT FOR?`

segments.voice: Take heed, he says, that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them. Don't sound a trumpet when you give, the way the hypocrites do, to be praised. Nobody's sure anyone literally blew trumpets; it's probably a vivid picture, like our blowing your own horn. Then, in the King James Bible: "But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth." Give so quietly that even you half forget it. The Greek word hypocrite is worth opening. Hupokrites meant a stage actor, someone who performed behind a mask. Jesus's point isn't about any one group. It's about anyone, in any faith or none, who performs goodness for an audience. And he says of them, three times: they have their reward. The Greek verb was used on receipts: paid in full. They wanted applause, they got it, and that's the whole payment. Then prayer: don't pray on street corners to be seen. Instead, in the King James Bible: "But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which is in secret shall reward thee openly." Closet here means an inner room, maybe a storeroom, the one room in a small house with a door. It doesn't mean praying together is wrong; Jesus prayed in the synagogue and taught his friends a prayer that begins our Father. It's about the audience. The same goes for fasting: wash your face, look normal, and let it be between you and God. Your Father sees in secret. The quiet good isn't wasted. It's seen by the one who matters.
screen: `NO TRUMPETS.` · `HUPOKRITES: AN ACTOR IN A MASK.` · `THEY HAVE THEIR REWARD: PAID IN FULL.` · `SHUT THY DOOR.` · then, large: `THY FATHER WHICH IS IN SECRET.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray behind a closed door. If you can, go into a room right now and shut the door. A bedroom, a bathroom, a parked car, anywhere with no audience. Sit down. Notice what it's like to be unseen. Nobody to impress. Nothing to perform. If you pray, you can speak to God here as simply as you'd speak to someone you trust. If you don't, just rest in the quiet, and let it be enough. The bell holds the time.
Not to be seen. Give, pray and fast without an audience, because the Father sees in secret.
Your line: the father sees in secret. Today, do one good thing and tell no one. Not now, not later. Let it stay between you and God. Day two hundred forty-eight.

howItsDone: This passage is read in many churches on Ash Wednesday, at the start of Lent, when Christians take up quiet giving, prayer and fasting; many give anonymously and keep a private time of prayer each day.

original.note: Greek: actor, one who plays a part. English hypocrite comes from it.

trapdoor: what you thought: hypocrite means someone who says one thing and does another.
what it means: someone who performs goodness for an audience, and gets the audience as their whole reward.
what a scholar hears: hupokrites is a stage actor; apechousin, they have, was a receipt word: paid in full.

notes: The outline range is 6:1–6; the script briefly adds fasting (6:16–18) since the index hook mentions it.
apecho as a commercial receipt term ('paid in full'), from papyri (Deissmann): confirm.
Trumpets: literal practice unattested; the script says 'nobody's sure'. Confirm.
Care taken that 'hypocrites ... in the synagogues' is not read as a charge against Jews: the script generalizes to 'anyone, in any faith or none'. Keeper to confirm.
tameion ('closet') as an inner room or storeroom: confirm. Ash Wednesday Gospel (Matthew 6:1–6, 16–21) in Catholic and RCL lectionaries: confirm.
